When I was twelve I went to Girl Scout camp, and one night the counselors told us the story of the "Lat Monster." ("Lat" being short for "latrine.") The story was, an unmarried woman who lived near the camp gave birth to a deformed baby (I don't remember if she was raped; probably not, seeing as how it was a Girl Scout camp), which she or her strict father saw as punishment for her unwed motherhood. The baby's knees and lower legs were backward, and the baby had eyes too far apart or something, a misshapen head. They shoved the baby into the basement, and there it lived, with them throwing food down at it regularly, for twenty-off years. Of course, there was no toilet in the basement, so the child grew up in its own waste. Because it never was exposed to the sun, its skin was horrifically pale, and it had weird patches of black hair all over it.

Anyway. The house burned down, killing the family, but the child, now a young man with serious mental issues and psychotic tendencies, survived. It escaped the basement and ran into the GS camp, where he noticed the smell of the latrines, which smelled like home. So he crawled down into the latrine pit and lived there during the day, coming out at night to search for food. Because of his pallor and dark patches on his skin, he was almost invisible in the latrine pit, and because his legs were backward, he couldn't run; he could only hop, taking big long leaps, very fast, and all that hopping made his legs super strong. At some point, he found a butcher's hook, and he would use it to grab some poor unsuspecting Girl Scout on her way to/from the latrines at night, drag her into the pit, kill her, and eat her.

This story terrified us all when they told it to us; we were afraid to leave our cabins at night (and most of us didn't sleep the night they told it to us, which also happened to be the night we slept in hammocks in the trees, completely exposed. It did not help that this was barely a decade after three Girl Scouts were murdered at a camp (those poor girls, it's a horrible story), and most of us only found out about that when we arrived at our camp.

It sounds ridiculous now, because it really was pretty ridiculous (Mr. Mantooth laughed his ass off when I told him the story years ago)...but it does mean that when I see fats with those backward-looking knees, I shudder, thinking of the Lat Monster leaping through the woods, leaving an ammoniac stench in his wake as he searches for food. Especially when I think about how unsanitary are the bathroom habits of pigs fat enough for the backward-knee effect, and how they must smell, and how they are constantly eating... Instead of Lat Monsters, we need to deal with Fat Monsters. They smell just as bad, and instead of a butcher's hook they kill you with their whining and screeching and demands.

It was genuinely terrifying while actually out camping in the woods, especially embellished as it was with the story of "a camper last year" who was o her way to the latrine one night when she thought she heard rustling in the trees; she stopped to listen, and moments later heard a soft thud behind her, followed by a whiff of eu d'latrine and what sounded like someone breathing carefully, trying to be quiet. She screamed and started running toward the cabins and (of course) the very counselor telling the story happened to be up and heard this, and thought he saw a shadow zipping through the trees for a moment before it disappeared. There was another anecdote about a girl using the latrine at night who heard sounds from one of the other stalls, a series of splashy sorts of movements, and that was pretty scary, too. I think a lot of us went home with minor UTIs, honestly, because the latrines were gross enough that we used them as little as possible already, without the additional deterrent of being terrified a deformed smelly cannibal was going to grab us and pull us down into the pit.

I have to admire the people who came up with the story, though. It has all the elements of a good scary campfire story: the hideous unwanted child locked away from human contact, growing up twisted and full of hatred in a body bizarrely deformed; the fire consuming a farmhouse (and there was a ruined house near the entrance to the camp, which all the buses drove past on arrival, so we'd all seen the burnt-out shell) and leaving only the hideous child alive; the meat hook; the abnormal movement/leaping through the forest; the idea of a killer undeterred by the nastiness of the latrine pit, happily living down there, lurking and watching you in your most vulnerable position; the additional vulnerability of having to walk some distance to use the bathroom at night, in the dark, through the woods--no plumbing in your cabin, and the cabins were really "permanent tents," which is to say a canvas tent topping a wooden half-wall and frame, not enough to keep anyone out... (Honestly, given the lack of real security at that camp [and other GS camps], it's kind of surprising that the Oklahoma murders in 1977 were the only violent events at such a camp.) Now that I'm thinking of it, I seem to recall the counselors mentioning something about food and supplies occasionally going missing or being deliberately left out in an attempt to appease the Monster and keep him from snatching any campers, and of course then there's the biggest fear, of being grabbed and killed by a stranger, especially being grabbed and taken to a horrible latrine to be killed.

Add all of that to the general creepiness of being in the woods at night, being away from home for an extended period for the first time for most of us, being girls at an age where you really start to feel and understand how vulnerable you are and how many dangers are truly out there, and being in an unguarded camp with a bunch of other girls, like a serial killer smorgasbord, and you have a recipe for a lot of sleepless nights.
